_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the 14 logged features, the rule engine, and feature normalization.
_do_not_edit_generated: Never hand-edit the generated files. Edit this spec and run tools/gen_engine.py, then tools/test_parity.py.
_model_input_note: All 14 features below are still SAMPLED, LOGGED, and kept in the database/CSV schema -- 'model_input' only controls whether a feature is fed to the neural network. A feature with model_input=false is still a real column (char_id, session_number, difficulty_level, prev_confidence, prev_mistakes, prev_accuracy, prev_mastery, current_streak, time_since_last_practice, hint_count): none of them are read by any rule below, so the model has nothing to gain from seeing them, and dropping them shrinks the input layer. Only the 4 features marked model_input=true are fed to the network: response_time, press_duration, retry_count, wrong_streak.

_feature_timing_contract.critical: Each feature is sampled at a specific moment. Web and firmware MUST sample at the same moments or the model misbehaves on hardware. The three groups:

pre_attempt.when: Read from stored history BEFORE this attempt is scored. These answer 'what did we know about this learner going in'.

post_attempt.when: Updated WITH this attempt's result, then read. This is the group that must not be sampled early.

_feature_timing_contract.correctness_is_derivable: There is deliberately no is_correct feature. Because the streaks are post-attempt, current_streak > 0 means the attempt just scored was CORRECT and wrong_streak > 0 means it was WRONG. They are mutually exclusive and exactly one is > 0 after any scored attempt.
_feature_timing_contract.why_it_matters: The rule engine branches on wrong_streak to decide REPEAT vs HINT. If the streaks were sampled pre-attempt, the engine would be branching on information the model cannot see in its input vector, and model accuracy would cap out for reasons that look like a training bug but are not.

features.name: char_id
features.desc: Index into data/braille_map.json letters[]. Not read by any rule -- logged for per-character analysis only.

features.name: response_time
features.desc: Audio prompt end -> submit button press. Clamped at max.

features.name: press_duration
features.desc: Mean press->release duration across the keys used in this attempt

features.name: retry_count
features.desc: Retries on THIS character within the current prompt

features.name: prev_accuracy
features.desc: Rolling accuracy on this character across all prior attempts. Logged only -- no rule reads it since WORD_PRACTICE (its one consumer) was removed.

features.name: prev_mastery
features.desc: Mastery score for this character (see mastery_update). Logged only -- WORD_PRACTICE/INCREASE_DIFFICULTY/the stale-gap rule, its only consumers, were all removed.

features.name: hint_count
features.desc: Hints used on this character within the current prompt. Logged only -- under the current rules it is an exact function of retry_count (hint_count = max(0, retry_count-1)), so it adds nothing as a separate model input.

features.name: session_number
features.desc: 1-based session index for this user. Not read by any rule -- logged for collection-progress analysis only.

features.name: difficulty_level
features.desc: Adaptive difficulty tier. No rule updates or reads it any more (INCREASE_DIFFICULTY/REVIEW_PREVIOUS were removed); kept as a logged column only.

features.name: time_since_last_practice
features.desc: Seconds since this character was last practiced. Clamped at 7 days. Logged only -- its one consumer (the stale-gap REVIEW_PREVIOUS rule) was removed.

features.name: prev_confidence
features.desc: Previous confidence state: 0 CONFIDENT, 1 HESITANT, 2 GUESSING. Not read by any rule -- logged only.

features.name: current_streak
features.desc: Consecutive CORRECT attempts on this character. >0 means the attempt just scored was correct. Logged only -- WORD_PRACTICE/INCREASE_DIFFICULTY, its only consumers, were removed.

features.name: wrong_streak
features.desc: Consecutive WRONG attempts on this character. >0 means the attempt just scored was wrong.

features.name: prev_mistakes
features.desc: Lifetime wrong attempts on this character, all sessions. Not read by any rule -- logged only.

_normalization_note: Fixed min-max scaling with clamping, using the min/max above. DELIBERATELY NOT dataset-derived: fixed ranges mean the ESP32's normalization can never drift from what the model was trained on, even when the dataset grows and the model is retrained. normalized = clamp((raw - min) / (max - min), 0, 1). Only applies to model_input features -- see _model_input_note.
_rules_note: Ordered list, FIRST MATCH WINS. All conditions in a rule are ANDed unless logic is OR. The final rule must have an empty condition list (the default).

teaching_action_rules.rationale: First wrong attempt on this prompt -- just try again, no help yet.

Still wrong after at least one retry on this prompt (retry_count>=1, since ta_repeat_on_first_wrong already caught retry_count==0). Keep helping on THIS character every subsequent wrong try, uncapped, rather than escalating to a different one -- REVIEW_PREVIOUS was removed because abandoning the current letter mid-struggle teaches nothing about the letter the learner actually needs.
wrong_streak==0, so the attempt just scored was correct -- move on normally.

confidence_rules.rationale: Many retries or a very long pause both read as guessing.

mastery_update._comment: Exponential moving average, applied AFTER each scored attempt. Shared by web, firmware, and the synthetic generator so mastery curves are identical everywhere. prev_mastery is no longer a model input, but it is still computed and logged (per-character analytics, and a candidate signal if a future rule set wants it back).
mastery_update.formula: correct ? m + alpha_correct * (1 - m) : m - alpha_wrong * m

session._comment: Definition of a session, so session_number and time_since_last_practice mean the same thing everywhere.
